firstCallNotes.buyerRole: VP Branch Operations with regional sales manager on the call.
firstCallNotes.pain: Counter reps are promising hose, fittings, and MRO parts before they know whether the local branch, another branch, or a supplier can actually fulfill the order.
firstCallNotes.proofRequested: Show a branch availability path that connects the customer promise, product SKU, replenishment action, and fulfillment support without turning it into manufacturing.
firstCallNotes.valueHypothesis: Reduce missed promises, speed counter-sales decisions, protect margin on urgent replacement orders, and make replenishment exceptions visible sooner.
firstCallNotes.competitorOrSpreadsheetPressure: They currently check branch spreadsheets, supplier portals, and a point inventory lookup before calling the customer back.
firstCallNotes.uncertaintyOrMissingEvidence: Website category evidence is thin; confirm the exact branch/category terms before claiming industry fit.

expectedStory.buyerProblemSummary: Gulfshore needs branch teams to make a believable availability promise while the buyer is still on the phone.
expectedStory.proofMove: Open the Product SKU, then show branch availability, replenishment timing, and fulfillment support as one NetSuite proof path.
expectedStory.objectionResponse: If they ask whether the promise is current enough, show the returned records first and ask which branch or supplier handoff they want to validate next.
expectedStory.competitiveContrast: NetSuite keeps branch promise, replenishment action, and order context together instead of stitching spreadsheets and supplier portals.
expectedStory.roiSafeValueFraming: Frame ROI as risk reduction: fewer missed promises, faster counter-sales decisions, and cleaner replenishment exception handling after the buyer confirms the baseline.
expectedStory.noClaimCaution: Do not claim measured ROI, manufacturing readiness, WIP, record creation, write actions, or guaranteed availability.
expectedStory.weakEvidenceConfirmationBehavior: Ask the consultant to confirm branch/category evidence before using ROI, competitive, or write-prep language.

firstCallNotes.buyerRole: Director of Sales with branch manager and inside sales lead.
firstCallNotes.pain: Contractors ask whether breakers, conduit, panels, and job-critical parts are available today, but reps do not trust the branch transfer and supplier ETA story.
firstCallNotes.proofRequested: Show availability, substitute/alternate readiness, and replenishment confidence for a contractor order without showing production or assembly language.
firstCallNotes.valueHypothesis: Win contractor trust by making the counter promise more precise, reducing callbacks, and protecting margin when urgent jobs need alternatives.
firstCallNotes.competitorOrSpreadsheetPressure: They compare against Epicor Eclipse reports, supplier portals, Excel branch transfer sheets, and customer texts.
firstCallNotes.uncertaintyOrMissingEvidence: Candidate pack is not source truth yet; use as review-only story expectations until human-reviewed pack approval.

expectedStory.buyerProblemSummary: MetroVolt needs counter reps to prove contractor-critical availability and alternatives before promising the job.
expectedStory.proofMove: Open the contractor Product SKU, then show branch transfer/replenishment support and fulfillment confidence for the order promise.
expectedStory.objectionResponse: If they ask how this avoids another callback, show the returned records and ask which alternate, transfer, or supplier ETA needs to be trusted before the contractor leaves.
expectedStory.competitiveContrast: NetSuite keeps contractor demand, item availability, branch transfer context, and fulfillment support in one path instead of splitting the story across Eclipse reports, supplier portals, and texts.
expectedStory.roiSafeValueFraming: Frame value as fewer callbacks, faster contractor counter decisions, and better margin protection after they confirm the current callback baseline.
expectedStory.noClaimCaution: Do not claim guaranteed delivery, measured ROI, manufacturing, WIP, write actions, or source-pack truth for the proposed electrical pack.
expectedStory.weakEvidenceConfirmationBehavior: Mark the electrical pack as review-only and ask for website/category confirmation before source mutation.

firstCallNotes.buyerRole: General manager with parts counter lead and service coordinator.
firstCallNotes.pain: Dealers lose customer confidence when mower, snowblower, attachment, and replacement-part availability differs between the sales counter, service desk, and supplier ETA.
firstCallNotes.proofRequested: Show dealer SKU availability, channel allocation, and service/parts fulfillment support for a customer order.
firstCallNotes.valueHypothesis: Protect seasonal revenue, reduce service desk escalations, and help staff answer whether they can sell, reserve, or replenish the item.
firstCallNotes.competitorOrSpreadsheetPressure: They use dealer management reports, OEM portals, QuickBooks exports, and whiteboard allocations during seasonal peaks.
firstCallNotes.uncertaintyOrMissingEvidence: Need website/category confirmation before claiming this is outdoor power specific rather than generic hardgoods.

expectedStory.buyerProblemSummary: Ridgeway needs one dealer-ready story for whether a product can be sold, reserved, replenished, or supported by service.
expectedStory.proofMove: Open the dealer SKU, then prove allocation, replenishment timing, and service support against the customer promise.
expectedStory.objectionResponse: If they ask what happens during a seasonal spike, show the proof path and ask which allocation or supplier handoff currently causes the most rework.
expectedStory.competitiveContrast: NetSuite keeps dealer demand, SKU availability, allocation, and service fulfillment visible instead of splitting it across DMS reports, OEM portals, and whiteboards.
expectedStory.roiSafeValueFraming: Frame ROI as seasonal risk reduction: fewer escalations, clearer allocation decisions, and faster customer answers after the baseline is confirmed.
expectedStory.noClaimCaution: Do not claim guaranteed seasonal availability, measured savings, manufacturing, WIP, write actions, or unsupported outdoor-power fit.
expectedStory.weakEvidenceConfirmationBehavior: Ask for dealer/category confirmation before using outdoor-power-specific claims.
